pr_body:
This moves `top_metrics` from global ordinals to segment ordinals which
should should speed it up a ton on shards receiving a lot of writes at
the cost of a little speed on shards that aren't receiving many writes.

The rally tests on hot shards so the performance cost is between .5% and
5%:
```
|                               |  before |  after  |   diff   |    |
|  50th percentile service time | 706.406 | 716.434 |  10.0277 | ms |
|  90th percentile service time | 738.705 | 742.636 |   3.9311 | ms |
| 100th percentile service time | 773.643 | 812.476 |  38.8331 | ms |
```

That seems worth it for 0 startup cost on hot shards.

Closes #70453
pr_title: Speed up top_metrics on hot shards
pr_comment: Hey Nik, sorry for the test failure. unmuted the test to collect more debugging information

> Hey Nik, sorry for the test failure. unmuted the test to collect more debugging information

Not at all!

> This looks good. I wonder if down the road it's worth having both segment and global ordinals modes, with an execution hint? IIRC, that's what we do in Terms family.

I don't think it's worth having a hint. At least, I hope it isn't. Its a bunch of extra code just to parse it and stuff. I was hoping we could get away without global ords at all here. But we need them I think we'd be better off with a heuristic to pick when the use them.

review_comment: Although this isn't literally an `instanceof` check, it's still relying on the class type to convey capabilities.  I wonder if we should add a `ValuesSource#hasSegmentOrdinals()` method to parallel the `hasGlobalOrdinals()` method we were using before this change?
I'll open up a follow up.
